title: Connected generic fibre of a flat degeneration over a DVR
statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring and f:X→Spec R a flat morphism with X connected and nonempty. If the scheme-theoretic closed fibre is reduced, the scheme-theoretic fibre over the zero prime is connected and nonempty. No finiteness or separatedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer π. On an affine open Spec A of X, flatness makes π a nonzerodivisor. The generic-fibre restriction is Spec A[1/π], and the closed fibre is Spec A/πA, which is reduced.

A nontrivial idempotent e on a disconnected generic fibre restricts on Spec A[1/π] to z/π^n. Choose n minimal. The idempotent equation implies z²=π^n z in A. If n>0, reducedness of A/πA forces z to be divisible by π, contradicting minimality. Thus the idempotent extends to A. This algebraic assertion is already proved as IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_eq_algebraMap_of_isIdempotentElem in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.DiscreteValuationRing.Basic.

Flatness makes the affine extensions unique. Restrict to affine opens in overlaps to see that they agree, and glue by the structure-sheaf axiom. Connectedness of X makes the resulting global idempotent zero or one, contradicting its generic restriction.

The generic fibre is nonempty: choose any point of the nonempty X and an affine neighbourhood Spec A. Flatness over the DVR makes A inject into A[1/π]; since A is nonzero so is A[1/π], whose spectrum supplies a generic-fibre point.
